asm/us/517A0.s is instruction-for-instruction identical to asm/us/yay0.s (Yay0_Decompress @ 0x8000B7F0): reads decoded size/link offset/chunk offset from header +4/+8/+C, walks control bits at +0x10, splits 16-bit link entries into count/offset (srl 12 / andi 0xFFF), and copies via LZ back-references. audio_commands.c:547's own comment says the operation is "Decompress first file Yay0 from gMoveSoundTempBuffer, into gSfxWaveTable", performed via Audio_CopyDataWithCacheSync → this function; the length argument is even ignored (size comes from the Yay0 header), so plain-copy semantics do not hold.

Claim 'packed normal vector representation' is false. The table is word 3 of the hardcoded ModelSegment gNormalModelSegment (src/audio_sfx_wrapper.c:10), i.e. ModelSegment.unk_0C (src/33FE0.h:74-85), and is consumed as the -1-terminated vertex link table: Model_BuildVertexRuntimeData walks its s16 entries until -1 to set each vertex's childIndex/parentIndex (src/33FE0.c:449-460), and the transform-command builder walks each vertex's parent run to enumerate blended vertex pairs (src/33FE0.c:1294-1306, `while (temp_v0_2 != -1)`). The data is vertex indices with 0xFFFF separators - e.g. gNormalModelNormals[1] = 0x3FFFF is the pair (3, -1) - sized for segment header word 0x000A0008 (10 vertices, 8 triangles, matching gNormalModelIndices[12] = 24 s16 = 8 triangles x 3); a packed-normal table would not carry -1 terminators, and vertex colors/normals live in the Vtx data (gNormalModelTextureCoords).

Claim 'RGB565 color entries for vertex colors' is false. The table is word 4 of gNormalModelSegment (src/audio_sfx_wrapper.c:10) = ModelSegment.tableSegment, and every reader passes it to Model_GetVertexJoint / Model_GetVertexClass / Model_GetVertexThreshold (src/33FE0.c:289-343), which use the per-vertex entry as an INDEX into the class lookup banks D_800763B0 / D_800765B4 / D_800769BC etc. (called at src/33FE0.c:436-438, :917, :1307-1313). Its values are per-vertex class ids for the 10 vertices (0xCE00CB = 206,203; 0xCA00CD = 202,205; ...), not colors; as RGB565 they would be near-black, and the model's vertex colors already live in the Vtx data at gNormalModelTextureCoords.

Claim 'packed normal vector representation' is false. Same defect as D_80077738/gNormalModelNormals: word 3 of gSpecialModelSegment (src/audio_sfx_wrapper.c:17) is ModelSegment.unk_0C, the -1-terminated vertex link/index table consumed by Model_BuildVertexRuntimeData and the transform-command builder (src/33FE0.c:449-460, 1294-1306); its data is identical vertex indices with 0xFFFF separators, not normals.

Claim 'RGB565 color entries' is false. Same defect as D_80077790/gNormalModelColors: word 4 of gSpecialModelSegment (src/audio_sfx_wrapper.c:17) is ModelSegment.tableSegment, feeding Model_GetVertexJoint/GetVertexClass/GetVertexThreshold class lookups (src/33FE0.c:289-343); its entries are per-vertex class ids, not RGB565 colors.

Claim 'vertical offset in distance calculations' is false. gSushiHeightOffset has a single use, and it is angular: SushiGame_ComputePlateDistance computes `var_fv1 = (0.5f * gSushiHeightOffset) + gSushiRotationAngle + (30.0f * ptr->unk_000)` (src/fragments/sushi_game/sushi_game_14A030.c:172) and feeds var_fv1 to SINS/COSS (:177-179) exactly like the conveyor slot angle in SushiGame_GetConveyorSlotPosition (:156-165, a degrees value wrapped at 360.0f); the resulting distance vector is horizontal with y = 0.0f (:178). The variable is a plate-angle bias (10.0f -> 5 degrees), not a height.

Claim 'vibrato current, target, and step values' misnames the mechanism: the struct at 0x800FCD98 is touched only by GbMusic_CmdPitchSlide (gb_audio.c:338-348, unk_0C=duration divisor, rotation=target note frequency via GbMusic_GetNoteFrequency, status|=0x10), GbMusic_StartPitchSlide (:708-717, posX=start frequency, RentalSlotAnimData_PosePhase=(target-start)/duration = per-tick step) and GbMusic_AdvancePitchSlide (:685-706, posX += step until the target is reached, then status &= ~0x30 stops it). That is a monotonic portamento/pitch slide with an explicit stop condition - vibrato (periodic oscillation) exists nowhere in the file. Every touching function is already named *PitchSlide*, so the variable contradicts its own domain. Companion type rename: VibratoState -> PitchSlideState (row below).

Same evidence as the gVibratoState row.

Claim 'stores sustain levels for each channel' is false: the u8[8] at 0x800FCE18 is written only by GbMusic_CmdSetDutyRotation (gb_audio.c:393-400, command 0xFC) and rotated by GbMusic_RotateChannelDuty (:719-730): the byte is rotated left 2 bits (value *= 4 then OR old top bits >> 6) and its top 2 bits are written to GetChannelRegister(arg0,1) = NRx1, the GB duty/length register. Claim 'stores tempo/speed modifiers for each channel' is false: the u8[8] at 0x800FCE20 is written by GbMusic_CmdSetDutyCycle (gb_audio.c:350-353, byte << 6 = duty bits in the top of NRx1) and GbMusic_CmdSetDutyRotation (:397, byte & 0xC0), then OR-ed into the NRx1 duty/length register by GbMusic_WriteChannelDutyLength (:595-607, sp1F |= tmp into GetChannelRegister(arg0,1)) and GbMusic_CmdPlayNoteWithDuty (:444-445). Renders GB channel 4 (noise), not channel 3 (wave): it reads gGbSoundRegs[0x10]-[0x13] = NR41-NR44 (register index = (addr & 0xFF) - 0x10 per GbAudio_QueueRegisterWrite, gb_audio_render.c:106; NR41-44 are the noise channel registers, 0xFF20-0xFF23), looks up gGbNoiseSampleTable[nr43 & 7][col] (:735, :744), and on expiry clears NR52 bit 3, the channel-4 status bit (`gGbSoundRegs[0x16] &= 0xFFF7`, :755/:760). In GbAudio_RenderSamples its output is gated by NR51 bit 3 (`tmp2 & 8`, the noise-channel enable) at gb_audio_render.c:229-231 — a wave channel would be bit 2 (value 4). The function's own locals (nr43/nr44) and comments ("NR42&8") already reference the NR4x noise registers; wave registers NR30-NR34 would be indices 0xA-0xE, which it never touches.

State of the noise channel, not the wave channel: gWaveState is used exclusively inside the NR41-NR44 channel-4 renderer (gb_audio_render.c:710-809) — sample id selected via gGbNoiseSampleTable (:744-748, Rom_DmaRead of gAudioSfxDataBuffer samples), divisor/scale from NR42/NR43 envelope (:766-770, `gWaveState.unk_14 = (NR42 & 0xF0) * fv`), length from NR44, and it is the struct whose expiry clears NR52 bit 3 (channel 4). No NR30-NR34 (wave) register is ever consulted; sampled "noise" playback via gAudioSfxDataBuffer, not a wave RAM sample index. Name kept distinct from the never-read gNoiseState at 0x800FCFB8 (see separate review row).

Static s16 gTexelsPerWord[] = {16, 8, 4, 2, 0, 0} at src/geo_render.c:107; its only uses are the row alignment tests in GeoRender_BindTexture (def :1218): temp_t0->posY % gTexelsPerWord[0] (:1236) and % gTexelsPerWord[temp_t0->TrainerSlotSaveData_GamePort] (:1242). Claim 'rotationX over pitch' misidentifies the variable: gDrowzeeCamRotationX (0x87B000F4) is the camera DISTANCE, not an X rotation. The pre-c7 name gDrowzeeCamPitch was equally wrong; c7 swapped terminology on a misidentified variable instead of fixing it.
